features: Remote purchases actually take the days the listing advertises: NPC Market buys schedule the card for its stated eta_days (1–10 game-days), buy-direct distributor orders ride one game-day on the truck, and BidBay snipes land in 1–2 game-days — cash leaves at purchase, the card admits to the vault when the parcel is due, and a full shelf holds it on the doorstep (vault admission retries each tick under the storage policy). All arrivals ride the game-day clock (12h or 24h per save setting). In-person buys — shop floor, conventions, estate lots, yard sales — stay instant because you walk out with the card. A new Inventory 📦 In transit tab lists every parcel with seller, channel, condition and a live game-day ETA; the Market card ETA now reads 'N game-days'; and the POST /api/market/deliver-due hook lets the client force the doorbell. Verified end-to-end on the rig: buy → in transit row with correct ETA → forced due → landed in the vault as a collection card. Also: BidBay seller-side transit was still a pre-clock relic (25/45/80 real seconds — parcels 'delivered' before the buyer finished paying); economy = 2 game-days, standard = 1, priority = half, scaled by the day-length setting

entries.title: Your clock, your call
features: Game day length is now a Settings option (Settings → Game pace): 12h — two game-days per real day, the default since v0.5.61 — or 24h — the classic pre-0.5.61 cadence rolling once per real day at 00:00 UTC. The choice is per save, takes effect at the next boundary, and everything follows it automatically because every day calculation reads one settings-backed accessor: the header day clock and DAY counter, the once-per-game-day gates (which stamp plain date keys again at 24h), grading/pawn/war/rotation durations, the client's ETA formatting, and the rebalanced 12h-era costs now stretch or halve with the same dial — at 24h a game-day costs twice the 12h-tuned amounts and grading takes twice the wall time, which is the original pre-rebalance economy exactly. Verified both modes live: the switch is instant via Settings chips or the API, boundaries and day numbers re-derive correctly in each, bad values are refused, and the pace panel's copy updates with the choice

entries.title: The 12h clock pays half rent
features: Daily costs rebalanced for the 12h game-day so real-world daily pressure stays where it was tuned: shop rents halve ($6 / $22.50 / $70 per game-day for hole-in-the-wall / storefront / flagship), franchise rents halve ($6 / $18 / $70 / $170), staff wages halve (buyer $4.50, grader $5.50, counter $2.50 base — manager and district/regional ladder wages too), business-loan and overdraft interest halves (0.6% / 1% / 1.75% by credit score, 2.5% overdraft), pawn-loan interest halves to 0.75% per game-day, the bare-card wear chance halves, and the disaster roll runs at half odds per game-day — twice the rolls, same real-day cost. One-time boot migration halves every stored wage (shop employees, franchise managers, the district and regional manager rows) and loan rate on saves that predate the switch, flag-guarded and idempotent — verified old-scale values halve exactly once and are untouched on rerun. Weekly bills (insurance, lockers, vault), Monday reports, taxes, and the real-world syncs stay on the real calendar, so the weekly squeeze is unchanged

entries.title: Two days a day
features: A game day is now 12 real hours instead of 24: the clock rolls at 00:00 and 12:00 UTC, so every real-world day holds two game-days and the whole daily heartbeat runs twice as fast — rent, payroll, loan interest, franchise rents, the condition-wear and disaster rolls, the save snapshot, achievements, and the morning-after day recap all fire at each boundary, the header day clock fills twice per day and the header DAY counter moves twice as fast, and grading turnarounds halve in wall-clock terms (express is back overnight; a standard 3–6 game-day job returns in 36–72h). All day math derives from one new shared clock module (server + client) — boundary, day number (day 1 = the game-day containing the save's creation), and day-key helpers — replacing the per-file UTC-date math; once-per-day gates now stamp a date-plus-half key ('2026-09-30-pm') and old date-only stamps read as their 00:00 boundary so a save's first afternoon re-rolls exactly once. Weekly bills (insurance, lockers, vault), Monday reports, month-end taxes, quarterly charges, the holiday calendar, rival war calendars, and the real-world price/catalog syncs deliberately stay on the real calendar — the 12h clock is the pace of daily life, not of the world's weekly scaffolding. Verified with boundary unit tests (11:59 vs 12:00 UTC split, day numbers across a boundary, legacy key parsing) and live on the rig: gates stamped '-pm', express 18h ETA reads ~2 game-days, standard stamped 3.6 game-days, daybar fraction correct

entries.title: Grading ETA tells the truth
features: The Inventory tab's at-the-grading-company row showed a submit-time relic: it still divided the remaining time by the old 20-second game-day that the great clock unification retired, so a real 1–2 day express job rendered as '~5535 game-days' (30.7 hours ÷ 20,000ms). The row now uses real UTC days like the Grading page, with the same hour/minute countdown formatting as the reveal gets close — the stored due date was always correct, only the display divided by a dead constant

entries.title: A reset rewinds the calendar
features: Resetting a save now rewinds the day counter to day 1: created_at IS the day number (day 1 = its UTC date), so reset re-stamps it to now and last_tick_at with it, so the next tick doesn't try to sim the whole rewind gap in one catch-up pass — the morning-after recap, the Today panel, and every day display agree on the fresh calendar. Daily gates come along: stale already-ran-today stamps from the pre-reset world (rolling snapshot, wear pass, disaster roll, payroll, quarterly license charge, the pending day-recap that would have posted a morning-after line about the wiped world) are cleared so the new day 1 arms them fresh instead of silently skipping rolls or posting a ghost recap. Verified on a day-13 rig save: reset lands on day 1 with $1,000 stable across ticks and the daily rolls re-armed for the new day

entries.title: A reset that resets
features: Reset save died halfway on any save with a yard sale: the wipe deleted yard_sales before its own yard_sale_cards child rows, SQLite threw FOREIGN KEY constraint failed, the endpoint 500ed — and because every earlier delete had already landed, the save was left half-erased with the old cash still in it, while the client toasted success. The whole wipe now runs child-before-parent inside one transaction: three more latent orderings fixed the same way (conventions before estate_lots, streams before stream_breaks and its spots/pulls, inventory before its binder_slots and vendor_sales — vendor_sales references both inventory and vendor_tables and now goes first), a mid-wipe failure rolls everything back instead of stranding the save, cash reliably lands at $1,000, and reset recreates the fresh save's Main Collection starter binder instead of carrying over empty shells. The client shows an error toast instead of silently claiming success. Verified against a seeded trap save (yard sale, convention + estate lot + vendor table chain, stream-break chain, binder with slotted cards): reset completes, cash is $1,000 immediately and stays there across ticks, every table wipes to zero, and a second reset is clean

entries.title: Grids that can't lie, art that won't quit
features: VirtualGrid reworked at the root so the collection can never overlap again: the scroll host used to carry the card grid class too, turning the whole virtual container into an auto-fill CSS grid — its spacer child collapsed into one ~188px column while the absolutely-positioned card window laid out multiple columns inside it, guaranteeing cell collisions (4 intersecting pairs measured on the live save). The host is a plain block now, the column count comes from a hidden probe grid that mirrors the density class at the real width, and — replacing the self-measuring probe cell entirely — row height is measured from the real rendered cells: the tallest cell in view sets the stride, re-measured whenever cells mount, the window resizes, or art finishes loading (an image growing its cell no longer leaves a stale pitch), and meta lines no longer wrap. Verified zero intersecting cells across every combination: comfortable/compact/list densities × flat and by-set browse × 800/965/1010/1400/1600px viewports, with per-section strides tracking their tallest cell (302/322px) and list rows holding at 66px

Missing card art got a fallback chain instead of a dead end: a transient CDN hiccup used to permanently kill that image for the session (the error state was sticky); now a failed thumbnail retries the derived pokemontcg.io URL for the same card id, then the original URL once more, before showing the error card — one flaky response no longer blanks a whole page of art

entries.title: Old saves heal themselves
features: Old saves with pre-split tournament history heal themselves on boot: the owner-stamp backfill could not tell which pre-split tournament pack sessions were yours versus the NPCs' — the old session ids carried no side marker, so tournament rips stayed in the player's records (40 of 60 rows on the first save that hit it) and had to be repaired by hand from the saved bracket. The migration now does that reconstruction itself: every played bracket slot records both sides' totals and each side's packs sum to those totals in cents, so the migration matches disjoint session subsets per slot, keeps whatever the __you__ side matched as the player's, stamps the rest 'other', and skips any slot it cannot fully resolve rather than guess. Runs once per save; verified to reproduce the hand repair row-for-row on the original unrepaired backup, to leave an already-healed save untouched, and to rerun as a no-op

Build fix: the installer smoke test was leaving its factory-fresh save in release/data after its own comment said it was deleted — every build since the leak began archived a junk 158MB 'played save' with zero inventory and could boot the game on a fresh $1,000. The smoke save is now actually removed; the played save is archived exactly once before the rebuild

entries.title: Papercuts, ironed
features: Pack Battles stopped crushing its two pickers at mid width: below ~820px of window the rival picker and product picker stack vertically (the same breakpoint rule every other two-column grid already had), and inside each row the rival's record badge stack and the product's stake column no longer shrink — at 965px wide the stake column keeps its 46px instead of clipping

The buylist offer sheet is now a pinned quote: selling sends along what the sheet showed, and if the shop's sheet moved in between (weekly want rotation, a copy re-graded) the sale is refused with the fresh number named instead of quietly paying different cents; the success toast reads the register total rather than the sheet, and a refused sale keeps your picks and refreshes the sheet

The buylist shop card no longer contradicts itself: 'pays ~75% cash · credit leg pays +8%' describes the credit bonus as the bonus it is, and 'no credit held' replaces the old 'no credit' that sat under a line advertising credit

Press Enter actually tears the pack now — the foil's keyboard hint used to require tabbing to focus the pack first; Enter works anywhere on pack openings, live-show reveal modals, and your duel-stage pack in battles (the rival's choreographed rip stays un-triggerable)

entries.title: Your pulls are yours
features: Pull History stopped claiming other people's cardboard: the always-on live wing writes every NPC host rip into pull_history, and battle opponents and tournament NPC matches rip there too — but the record endpoints read the whole table, so a fresh save that had opened one $4.49 pack showed 'ALL-TIME BEST PULL $413.66' and 'BEST PACK ON RECORD $625.94' from NPC shows the player never touched. Every rip row now carries an owner stamp ('player' or 'other'), Pull History, the all-time best pull, the best-pack banner, and the session cards read player rows only, and existing saves get their history backfilled by session-id shape (1,107 NPC rows stamped on the test rig, zero false positives)

Ownership rules: NPC live-show rips, packs NPC winners ripped on stream, team-break spot pulls, battle opponents' sides, and tournament NPC matches are world-log only; your own opens, your own-channel stream rips, your own tournament and battle rips, and rip-it-or-ship-it packs YOU won and chose to rip on stream all stay yours

entries.title: Everything in register
features: Fixed the card density bug for real: VirtualGrid now measures itself in place — a hidden probe cell mounted inside its own column, remeasured on every resize — so virtualized rows stay in register at any window width. The old hardcoded constants were wrong at real widths (rows drifted 263px apart under ~230px cards, compact claimed a fake 5 columns), which showed up as overlapping cards and blank bands in Collection, Set Detail, and Inventory

Pack battle pricing stopped charging for cardboard nobody rips: versus stakes are now the ripped share of the product (1 pack of a booster box run, 3 of a bundle, 9 of an ETB) instead of the full sealed price — a Surging Sparks booster stakes $4.49 a side, not $130+ — and both sides always rip the same product

Tournament entries are flat now: the Mini Invitational costs $25 and the Grand Slam $60, period. The old math staked 1.5x a randomly-picked ETB from every synced set, so entering could cost anywhere from $80 to $450 and each round ripped a different random product

The Buylist is rebuilt: shop picker cards show each store's flat rate and credit bonus, the want list shows what they'd actually pay per card, and the offer sheet got real column headers (Card / Market / They pay / %) with aligned rows, pick-all, and the SELL / SHOP tabs — no more flat wall of cluttered rows

Storage and Auctions is unlocked from the start (it was gated behind 5 sales for no good reason — you need storage space long before your 5th sale), and the capacity strip now appears below 60% full instead of waiting until 75%

entries.title: Show your work
features: Every deal badge now shows its work: a 'priced vs LP' (or MP/HP/NM) trust line sits under each Market badge, and BidBay badges carry 'vs {condition}' inline — so a condition-anchored comparison is explicit instead of implied

Hover a trust line and it names where the anchor comes from — live TCGplayer market, PriceCharting, Cardmarket trend, the simulated market, a comparable-based estimate, or real PSA comps for graded lots

entries.title: The badges tell the truth
features: Deal labels stopped lying about condition: the Market page anchored every listing against an NM price no matter the card's condition, so a fairly-priced LP (0.8×) read 'BELOW MARKET' and a fair HP (0.5×) read '🔥 BELOW MARKET −50%' — the anchors now apply the same condition multipliers the listings are priced with, so a badge means what it says

BidBay's NPC hunt had the same lie baked in: LP/MP stock priced off the NM market manufactured fake DEALs (fair MP asks reading '−35% DEAL') and fake MARKETs on overpriced LPs — spawn pricing and stored anchors are condition-aware now, and legacy rows re-anchor to the card's current real market at read time
Audited the rest of the scene: convention dealer tables, the estate floor, and Local Deals already anchored condition-aware — those badges were honest and are untouched

entries.title: No secrets about the clock
features: New 'Game pace' panel in Settings lays out exactly what one game day means for every system: rent and payroll at midnight UTC, daily interest, wear and disaster rolls stamped at midnight, the once-a-day save snapshot (with your last one), weekly bills on their own draft clocks, grading turnaround in real days, and the day-recap line — plus an explicit note that the real-world data syncs run on their own schedules, not game days
The panel shows YOUR numbers where it can — your actual shop rent and tier, your last snapshot moment — so pace is transparent rather than described

entries.title: Grading runs on the real clock
features: Grading turnaround now runs on REAL game days — the same UTC days rent, payroll, wear, snapshots, and the header day clock gate on. Express is genuinely 1–2 days and Standard genuinely 3–6; the old build used a pre-unification 20-seconds-per-day relic, so '2 game days' finished in about a minute while the day clock barely moved
The 'Back in' column now reads honestly: game-days at range, then hours, then minutes as your slab approaches the mailbox — legacy in-flight submissions still resolve exactly as before

entries.title: The buzzer steal
features: SNIPE: in the final 2 seconds of a sudden-death lot the BID button becomes a red ⚡ SNIPE — fire it and you take the lot OUTRIGHT at current + $1, no NPC counter-bid; that's the reaction play the real rooms reward. Too early and it lands as a normal bid (the window hadn't opened), too late and the hammer's already down — race-guarded against the 2.5s server heartbeat so a heartbeat-late snipe cleanly loses

The Today panel has moved off the Home dashboard: the day-clock hover dropdown is now the only Today surface, refreshed on every hover (the panel was doing double duty with the dropdown since v0.5.44)

entries.title: Real sudden death
features: $1 sudden death rebuilt to the real format: ONE card on screen at a time — $1 opens, a hard 6–10 second clock that no bid can extend, and at 0:01 the card is gone. Cards run cheap-to-rich so the rip's hit closes the sequence as the climax; you blink, you lose it (the old build put the whole pack on the block at once with rolling-hammer extensions)

Room heat is capped in DOLLARS, not multiples: the chase tops out a few dollars over market on commons and roughly $10–30 over on the grail — bids past that line just don't land, and NPC snipers obey the same ceiling (verified: commons at $0.89 market war'd to $2; a $3.50 card went $8 after 7 bids; zero over-cap sales across a full sequence)
A $1 opener always finds a taker — passed lots don't exist in this format — and the room runs on its own 2.5-second server heartbeat so 6–10 second lots actually live and die in real time

entries.title: The catalog ships with the game
features: A 14MB offline catalog seed (all 176 sets, ~20,600 cards, the latest real price for every card) now ships inside the installer and absorbs into any save on boot in seconds — fresh installs start fully stocked with real prices, and saves caught mid-crawl (API outages had been leaving sets undone, forcing a fresh crawl on every restart) top up instantly with zero API requests

The API stays for what it's actually for: a weekly delta pass brings new releases and changed sets, and the daily owned/wishlist price refresh keeps your cards current — the endless boot-time re-crawl is gone

Sealed pricing fix: in-print sets now sell at retail (MSRP) instead of chase-card expected value — 30th Celebration packs were pricing at the $30 EV cap against a real $4.49 shelf price; the pull-EV estimate only takes over once a set is actually out of print, so collector appreciation still works (151, Crown Zenith, Base, Celebrations unchanged)

entries.title: The morning after
features: A day-recap line lands in the activity feed at every UTC midnight rollover: what fired, what each roll cost, and the new day number — '🌅 Day 12 begins. shop rent -$45.00 ✓ · loan interest -$2.01 ✓ · disaster roll didn't roll. Day cost: -$47.01.' — so the morning-after view lives in the feed, not just in the Today panel's checkboxes

The recap keeps a rolling snapshot of the Today panel through the day and posts the final picture once after rollover (before the new day's systems stamp over it), posts nothing when the save sat closed for days, and never duplicates

entries.title: Hover the day
features: The header day clock is now a hover dropdown: resting on the DAY chip (or the final-hour ROLLS IN countdown) opens a mini Today panel — every roll due at midnight with its checked-off state, amounts in red, the weekly watch list, and the day's known-out total, refreshed on every hover so the checkboxes are honest even across midnight
The dropdown's 'Full Today panel →' button hops straight to the Home dashboard, and the countdown in the dropdown header always agrees with the chip above it

entries.title: Every channel is a real show
features: The seven channels now run their real formats end to end: tapping a channel swaps the FULL room — host header, chat, and that format's rails — not just a banner, so a $1 sudden-death room is all $1 lots, the mystery channel is all boxes, and the break rooms are all boards

Every channel rips its own product like real channels: the $1 rooms run the cheapest boosters on the shelf (a buck a card has to make sense), the vintage auction room rips the priciest, and the break / rip-it-or-ship-it / mystery rooms take a mid-tier modern product

A dedicated mystery-box channel is born: SlabDaddyDee's room becomes sealed boxes where a hit-bearing rip becomes a PREMIUM box (the hit buried under half the bulk) with a standard filler box alongside — every rip is buyable, nothing bleeds onto the rails

Format taglines in the show's welcome chat and LIVE feed lines ('every card $1 — sudden death, no mercy'), format names on every channel chip and tooltip, and page copy that names the whole format roster

entries.title: The last hour warning
features: The header day clock now warns before midnight UTC: in the final hour the DAY chip flips to a live ROLLS IN m:ss countdown with a slow amber breathing glow, and the last 10 minutes escalate to a fast red pulse with a red-haloed progress bar — rent, condition wear, disasters, and the save snapshot never land unseen
The countdown targets the same midnight as the Home Today panel (the two agree to the minute), and the countdown tooltip names what's about to fire and points at the Today panel

entries.title: Know what's coming
features: New Today panel on the Home dashboard: every roll that lands at the next UTC midnight in one list — shop rent with its amount (and the waiver when the cases sit empty), staff payroll, daily loan interest, the save snapshot, condition wear, and the disaster roll — each row checked off ✅ and struck through the moment it fires, on the same day-keys the systems themselves write

A weekly watch list below the dailies: the insurance premium with its next draft, locker rent, the vault rider, and franchise-store rent plus wages — so the bills that don't land at midnight still have a place on the board
Panel header counts down to the next roll (the same midnight the day clock runs toward) and totals the day's known out across every pending row with a dollar amount

entries.title: Nobody sleeps, nothing closes
features: The live wing is always on: every host runs a channel around the clock — seven rooms live at once, mid-rip whenever you open the page (was: two 3-hour windows a week, one show at a time). Rooms wrap and re-arm themselves, so the lineup rolls over constantly and never goes dark
Rips run at ~90s across all rooms — drops flash, hammers roll, and mystery piles open continuously across the whole platform, not just in the room you're watching

The Auction House has constant influx: the house keeps a rolling floor of ~10 live lots (target wobbles 7–13 so the room breathes), spawning up to two per tick with tighter windows — something is always starting and something is always about to hammer, on every visit
New CHANNELS lineup bar on the Live page: every live room as a chip with viewers, rip progress, and a live dot — one click hops to another host's room, and the whole thing is visible on every visit

entries.title: Watch the day turn
features: New top-right day clock: DAY n sits beside cash in the header with a progress bar that fills through the day — you can see the next daily roll (rent, condition wear, disasters, and your save snapshot) coming, instead of it landing unseen while you read a table
The bar ticks locally every 15s and the tooltip counts down to midnight UTC (the hour every daily system gates on); day 1 is the UTC day the save was created

entries.title: The 6 AM crew
features: Weekend flea markets: flat-price junk bins (25¢, 50¢, $1, $2, $5) where every card costs the bin price and a few are real cards that don't belong — the 25¢-for-a-shadowless fantasy, with comps that are honest, verifiable app prices

The grounds open at 6 AM and the NPC pickers are already there: every game tick they take 1–12 of the best remaining cards (highest value first, with a casual hand), so bins visibly drain while you read the table — the score you're chewing on can vanish next tick
Per-bin heat counter shows how many 20×+ cards are still buried, and when a picker pulls a real score the feed tells you exactly what you missed — FOMO is the mechanic

Digging is one blind card per click, revealed after you commit, logged to a Your Digs scrapbook with the multiple; Condition Wars rides along silently — the bin never shows the copy's sub-grade, your eye stays the edge

entries.title: Condition Wars
features: The hidden copy war goes public: every raw copy now rolls a fourth sub-stat — the print line, the row of ink dots across the artwork — and 92% of copies strike clean while a cursed few carry a below-the-eye-line smudge that caps any grade

Condition comps: card detail now shows what the MARKET pays for your exact copy — band value, this-copy value, and a drifted comp window — because two NM copies of the same card are not the same card and buyers know it

Sub-grade drift: once a copy's read is published (listed, stocked in a case, or offered to a buylist) buyers pay the copy's sub-grade, ±8% around the band — a clean strike earns a premium, a snow-capped edge sells at a discount. Unseen copies still price at the band: the information IS the value

The eye trains on looks now, not just grading results: every inspect counts (90 points to master, grades teach double), and your read persists per copy as its public face — plus a plain-language verdict (dead-centered, heavy whitening, visible print line) with the ± error shown

entries.title: The save that can't be lost twice
features: Rolling in-app save backups: the game photographs its entire save — cash, collection, sealed, every history — once per game day and keeps the last three, so a save-ruining mistake now costs you back to yesterday instead of everything

New Settings → Save backups panel: the snapshot list shows each save's moment (cash, cards, sealed, size), a 📸 Snapshot now button, and one-click Restore with a confirm dialog that tells you exactly what you're rewinding to

Restores run on sqlite's own online-backup API — no locks, no restart, the game just continues from the snapshot's moment — and every restore first parks a safety copy of your current world, so even a restore can itself be undone
Snapshots are plain single-file databases (portable, openable in any SQLite browser) and live in data/backups next to the save

entries.title: Insured for what it's worth
features: Fixed the insurance appraisal pricing sim-market cards at $0: the appraiser only read TCGplayer rows, so a collection held while external price APIs were dry (everything priced by the simulated market, the same numbers the shop grid shows) appraised to nothing and every weekly premium collapsed to $0/wk

The appraisal now walks the full price ladder per card — TCGplayer → PriceCharting → eBay → Cardmarket → simulated — so premiums track what your cards are actually worth at any price tier, and claim-victim selection and wear-loss math ride the same ladder (a sim-priced card can finally be a real claim)
Verified on a copy of a real save: 60 mostly sim-priced cards now appraise at ~$600 instead of $0 — Starter $0.63/wk, Collector $0.98/wk, Museum $1.40/wk

entries.title: The whole box, ripped
features: Booster bundles, ETBs, and displays open every pack in the box — a bundle is 6 real rips, a display 36, not one lonely pack at box price (the old code charged you for the box and handed you a single pack, a 6–36× value laundering)

Each pack in the box gets its own pull-history session, so the best-pack-total record stays an honest per-pack number — a 36-pack display can't fake-beat the record with one giant sum (the ceremony compares the best single pack of the box)
The ceremony announces the box: the foil reads 6 packs · 60 cards, the summary shows the full card count against the box price, and Inventory's button says OPEN BOX · 6 packs instead of OPEN 1

entries.title: Best pack ever
features: A second chase joins the record books: the best single-PACK total (the whole rip's worth, not just its top card) — beat it and the ceremony wears its own 📦 BEST PACK EVER banner in violet with a violet edge glow, the summary adds a struck-through BEST PACK BEFORE stat, and quiet sessions show the standing record instead
The two chases stack: a pack that sets both records runs the gold and violet glows together and flies both banners — verified live at +611% ROI

Every rip surface chases both records: Pack Battles duels and tournament rounds (with per-pack totals straight from the server, so a bundle can't smuggle a two-pack sum in), and Live Shopping stream rips and mystery piles

The bars come from one endpoint now: /api/pulls/best returns the card record and the best session total (sessions are one pack everywhere — battles and tournaments roll one session id per rip), each fetched BEFORE the open so a session can't beat itself

Pack Shop's BUY 1 & OPEN now hands its purchase to the full ceremony — it opens server-side first, so records could fall with no ceremony to see them; the handoff survives React StrictMode's double-mount

entries.title: Records fall everywhere
features: Pack Battles joins the record chase: a pull on YOUR side of the duel that beats your all-time best fires the full celebration — the tear stage's edges catch the gold glow and the 👑 NEW BEST PULL banner names the card that did it, in both Versus duels and tournament rounds (the rival's packs never steal your moment)
Live Shopping rips can make history too: a rip-it-or-ship-it win the host rips on stream, or a mystery pile you paid for, glows the compact tear overlay and banners the record before the reveal lands

The bar is read before the rip on every surface — the server writes battle/rip pulls during the call itself, so the record is fetched first (the same ordering bug the Pack Opening ceremony had was waiting in both new paths)
Honest negatives stay silent: verified that rips under the bar ($1.09 best) produce no banner, no glow — the celebration only exists for the record moment

entries.title: The record has a home
features: The all-time best pull is a permanent fixture now: Pull History opens with a gold-crowned ALL-TIME BEST PULL panel (card art, name, rarity, set, pull date, and the record value), and the Home dashboard's Collector record carries a compact 👑 Best pull on record row right between your KPIs and the gainers — both link to the card detail like every other card surface
The record endpoint grew up: /api/pulls/best now joins card name, image, set, rarity, and pull date instead of just an id and a number

Fixed the router eating another hidden view: #/pulls-history — the destination of the ceremony summary's View pull history button — has been bouncing home since v0.5.6's unknown-view guard, same shape as the #/opening fix

entries.title: The record run
features: Beating your best pull on record is a moment now: the screen edges catch a pulsing gold fire the instant the record card reveals, a 👑 NEW BEST PULL banner names the number, and the session summary strikes through your old PREVIOUS BEST while the record card wears a 👑 BEST crown and a gold halo of its own

The comparison is honest by construction: the all-time best is read before the pack is opened (the server writes the session's pulls during the open call, so any later fetch would compare the session against itself), and ordinary sessions that don't beat the record show nothing at all — the flourish only exists for the record moment
New /api/pulls/best endpoint backs the chase — the all-time single-card record lives in pull_history and now has a UI that cares about it

entries.title: The rip has a voice
features: The ceremony sounds like cardboard now — all synthesized in WebAudio, zero audio files: the foil crinkles while you pull the tear line (friction scales with how fast you pull), the rip gives way with a bright tear-and-give sweep, a two-note chime rings under the spark burst, and every reveal lands its own stinger scaled to the pull — a bright ding for hits, a two-note fanfare for HUGE, a boom-and-arpeggio for MASSIVE pulls (ordinary commons stay silent so the reveal keeps its calm)
The duel gets the treatment too: Pack Battles fires the resolution stinger at both-packs-open, scaled to your side's total — a win with a hit in it sounds like one
New Ceremony sound toggle in Settings (muted state remembers per browser), and every voice no-ops cleanly when muted — muted players get the exact same ceremony, just silent

entries.title: Every rip is a ceremony
features: The interactive tear-open pack is one shared component now, and every rip in the game goes through it: Pack Battles puts both packs on the table — you tear yours (pointer or keyboard), the rival's rips itself open a beat later, then the duel resolves; Live Shopping rip-ship wins and mystery piles land a compact tear overlay before the reveal modal, so the host's pull is something you open, not a list that appears

Battles and Live Shopping packs wear their set's real symbol too (Battles already carried symbol_url; the live-show serializer now joins it from the sets table), so a rip reads the same on every surface
Skip paths everywhere: Space or double-click skips the duel tear, skip-animation mode auto-rips Pack Opening packs, and the Live overlay obeys the same TearPack interactions as everywhere else

entries.title: Set foil & sparks
features: The tear ceremony learned three tricks: the pack is focusable and rips on Enter or Space (proper role, aria-label, and a yellow focus ring — the ceremony is keyboard-complete), every set's foil carries its own symbol as the pack art (emoji fallback when a symbol image is missing) with a deterministic per-set accent glow, and the finished rip throws a 16-spark burst in the house palette before the first card flies
Same set, same look: the pack hue is hashed from the set name, so a 30th Celebration pack reads differently from a Pitch Black one at a glance — and always the same way

entries.title: Rip it yourself
features: The pack opening is interactive now: before any card reveals, the foil pack exists on screen — hold it and pull down to tear it open, a glowing tear line riding your pointer with the crimped top peeling as you go; release past the middle and the rip finishes with a flourish, let go early and the foil snaps back shut. A Tear it open button does the pulling for you, and Skip-animation players get their packs auto-ripped

The game window is a normal taskbar citizen again: the app icon lives on the taskbar where players expect it, minimize minimizes, and X quits for real (stopping the server) — the tray icon stays on as a convenience for bringing a buried window back, not as a hiding place. Deep-linking to the pack-opening ceremony works again too: the router's unknown-view guard has been bouncing #/opening home since v0.5.6, so Buy 1 & OPEN opened your pack server-side and dumped you on Home
Fixed the Pack Shop's BUY 1 & OPEN flow landing on the ceremony (see above) — the reveal, summary, and pull history were all intact, just unreachable from the button that promised them

entries.title: The unwatched till
features: Dead hours are real now: the shop keeps a pulse after close (the closer rings stragglers, night traffic up from a near-zero 0.02×), and "unwatched" finally means unwatched — the skim keys to the wall-clock night band (21:00–06:00, ramping from close to deep night) instead of the traffic curve, which made 2am the only hour anyone could ever skim and left the mechanic firing in practice never. Cheap managers now skim a real 1–2% of gross at night, and the satellite till audit finally has something to catch

Loyalty reshaped to pay honestly: a checked-out manager leaks (up to 1.3×, and doesn't watch their own till) while well-paid loyalty buys a flat honesty floor — the old curve quietly rewarded keeping managers underpaid, since skimming only ever pays the owner back half

Fixed: the same local Sunday could pay the district or regional office twice — the weekly payroll guards keyed their once-per-day marker on the UTC day while the is-it-Sunday check read the local day, and every local Sunday spans two UTC dates (invisible in normal play, the night-sampling audit hit it weekly)
Fixed a stray per-skim console.log that fired in production

Doors tuned under the honest clock: walk-in base 0.06 → 0.08 and storefront rent $45 → $36/day, because the old sim numbers were measured at a permanent 18:30 peak pin — sim-audited, a fair-managed 3-door chain compounds at +$26/day with the full-day clock (per-door +$36–41), and the franchise audit now shows the real honesty gradient (1★ 1.7% skim → 5★ 0%)
The sims tell the truth about time now: SIM_HOUR=fullday spans the whole clock each simulated day (with a genuine late-night slice), and both sim:empire and sim:franchise run it

entries.title: The chain pays
features: Raise demands anchor to the market ladder now: a busy manager asks within reach of what their stars are actually worth (capped at 1.3× market, tapering as headroom runs out) — the old ask-anything game ratcheted a fair-run 3-door chain's payroll up ~45% in two months and turned decent management into a −$108/day drain

Loyalty pays in traffic, not just trust: loyal managers pull up to +20% more regulars (was +10%), so an attentive owner's doors gross ~$107/day against ~$93 under neglect — the sim now shows the honest trade-off: grant every raise and the chain compounds at +$39/day; ignore every ask and you keep ~$58/day but bleed 37 resignations a run and ~15% of door traffic

The management layer got lighter: the district ladder dropped to $15–42/day (was $18–55) and regional to $24–64 (was $30–82), so offices on a 3-door chain cost ~$92/day instead of $131, and satellite doors tick busier (walk-in base 0.05 → 0.06)

New full-empire audit `npm run sim:empire` (flagship + 3 satellites + DM + regional, built through the real gates): it plays the owner side of the raise game — attentive (grant everything) or negligent (ignore everything) — reads office costs from the ledger instead of end-of-run state, and counts 🚪 walkouts; the audit found the drain, this patch is the fix, and the audit confirms the fix

entries.title: Pro at work
features: Manager quality pulls real traffic now: the regulars-come-to-see-a-pro draw widened from ±12% to ±25% across the 1★–5★ band — a 5★ manager out-earns a 1★ by ~$22/day, more than covering the wage ladder, and a cheap hire visibly drags the door

Storefront satellites tuned to the break-even band: a well-run store nets about +$8–29/day by manager quality (sim-audited average +$16/day), instead of the old spread where quality barely mattered and every store landed within a few dollars of the same line

sim:franchise reports honest per-store net/day now (the old summary divided a whole run's drift by one day), and cross-band runs prove stocking strategy: mid-band stock carries the store, dollar-bin filler loses ~$55/day under the same rent

entries.title: The audit bench
features: Two new economy audits beside the rival sim: `npm run sim:franchise` replays the real chainTick across manager qualities (sales/day, skim%, rent+wage burden per ★), and `npm run sim:resale` plays a scripted flipper through the real deal flow (deal volume, expiry, ask-vs-value, instant-flip ROI) — both on throwaway database copies with the same isolation guarantees (bootstrap-first temp home, refusal guards, boot-file mirroring)

Fixed resale lot valuation: the deal generator sampled ANY price row for a card — including simulated-market rows — while the game realizes prices from TCGplayer data, so holo-only promos were valued at a fraction of what they actually pay (a measured 2.4× windfall on instant flips; audit ROI fell from an impossible +346% to the intended edge at +75%)
Resale lots now book their real condition: asks were discounted for LP/MP/HP copies but every card was stored as NM, quietly laundering worn cardboard into near-mint dealer payouts

entries.title: Nerve of steel
features: Outlasting a price war pays: when a war expires on the calendar — you held your prices, never matched, never flinched — the shop earns +2 reputation and the feed names it ("the block watched you hold your nerve through the whole fight")
The blink pays nothing: a rival that folds early surrenders the word-of-mouth to no one, so the three war outs now carry real trade-offs — wait for rep, match for traffic, buy for the block

Simulator hardening (found the hard way): the sim's temp-home redirect now happens before any database import (the old ordering silently ran sims against the real save), with a refusal guard, a `sim:rival` bootstrap that mirrors the boot files, and cross-run feed leakage cleaned

entries.title: Funded to fight
features: Price wars start funded: the rival's owner drops a $60 war chest in the register when a war is declared, and the fight now runs to its planned end on the calendar instead of collapsing into an early fold

The blink is a last resort now, not the routine exit: the fold threshold dropped to a truly dry till ($60 → $25) with half the old odds — a 30-day simulation went from 89% of wars ending in blinks to 0%, with 90-day runs at 4%
Wars last the same length as before (~5 days); there are just more of them, because a funded rival stays feisty — the same per-war drama, more often, and tills end healthier (30-day floor $122 vs $0)

entries.title: The ledger and the stake
features: The rival's till can't owe money anymore: wages stop mattering when the wallet is empty (a 90-day simulation ran broke rivals into −$1,900 of debt under the old math)

A broke, humbled rival with empty cases gets an owner stake — the owner dips into savings (up to 3 times) to restock and keep the comeback arc alive, instead of deadlocking forever with no cash to restock and no stock to sell

Fixed the humility bar: the comeback target is the rival's PRE-blink reputation now, not the post-retreat number — a blink used to start a "comeback" that was already finished (avg 0.6 days under the flag)
New headless simulator (server/scripts/rival-sim.ts): replays the real rivalTick() across whole simulated days on a throwaway database copy — the audit harness that found all three of the above

entries.title: Humble pie
features: The rival has a comeback arc now: after blinking first it eats humble pie — no new wars, and its fresh stock prices to sell (≈1.02× market instead of ≈1.22×) — while a reputation point a day (when the till can breathe) rebuilds toward its old pride
When the rep recovers, the humility lifts with a 😤 feed warning: "the till recovered, the rep rebuilt, and your window displays are being sized up again" — a blinked-out rival isn't a beaten one
The rival panel carries a 🩹 humbled badge while the peace lasts, and buying the rival out clears the state with everything else

entries.title: The right cardboard
features: War-price memory is keyed by card instead of database row: a blink restore (or a war expiring) can no longer nudge the ask of a different card the rival restocked into a freed slot mid-war — rows get reused, the cardboard doesn't
The restore also heals whole-stock dupes: every row of the war's card walks back to its pre-war ask together, while rows genuinely sold mid-war still miss it

entries.title: The till runs dry
features: The rival can blink first now: when its till runs dry mid-war, the cuts come off its cases (walked back to their pre-war prices), the war ends early, and the block notices the retreat — −2 reputation and a 🏳️ feed line. Starving them out is finally a strategy, not just a slogan

Wars now remember their pre-war prices: when a war naturally expires the rival walks its cuts back up instead of quietly selling at war prices forever, and rows it sold mid-fight simply miss the restore
The war banner tells you the third way out — "starve it and they'll blink first, match the cuts and meet them in the mud, or buy the block"

entries.title: Meet them in the mud
features: New ⚔️ Match their price button in the rival's war banner: one click reprices every contested case down to the rival's number — the margin goes, the walk-ins stay — and the war ends at parity (the war feed always promised "match them and lose margin"; now there's a button that actually does it)
"Undercuts you" badges clear at parity: a rival case only carries the badge while its ask sits under both the market and your live price on the same card, so a matched shelf reads as peace, not war
Matching when nothing is contested (or no rival stands across the street) answers honestly instead of pretending — the button never raises your prices to "match"

entries.title: The war that finally ended
features: Price wars across the street actually end now: an expired war stands down on the next day-tick with the "restocked at sane prices" feed line — the war-over check was logically unreachable, so a declared war used to run forever
The rival's till is honest again: restocking from it debits what the stock costs (the daily write-back was clobbering the restock purchase, handing the rival free inventory and an endless war chest)

The rival block audited end-to-end on live saves: wars only fire when the rival can actually undercut one of your cased cards, walk-in poaching deepens while a war runs (and vanishes when they close), the buyout escalates ×1.25 per lowball up to 3× their book, and buying the block books the fixtures-and-goodwill premium as overhead

entries.title: The overflow & the bill
features: Vault slots now prioritize: your most valuable slabs ride the glass first, and the overflow — slabs beyond the rider's 25 slots — sleeps at home where disasters can reach it (a break-in that finds the vault stocked now tells you exactly how many overflow slabs are still exposed)
The Storage page warns the moment slabs exceed vault coverage — "2 slabs beyond the vault slots sleep at home" — and the Insurance panel names which side every slab sleeps on
New 🛡 protection rollup on the weekly P&L: insurance premium + locker rent + vault rider in one line, so the price of safety is finally a number you can read at a glance
The Sunday business digest carries the week's protection cost too — a pure protector with no shop still gets their 🛡 line

entries.title: The collector's floor
features: Auto-scrap gets a value floor: set a dollar amount and cards worth more than it are collector cardboard, not filler — never sold for room, no matter how full the shelf gets (0 = no floor, the old behavior)
The floor editor lives right under the overflow policy on the Storage page, with a live badge showing the active floor and a one-click clear

The ♻️ pre-flight hint turns into a red ⚠️ warning when the floor blocks a buy — "the $5 floor blocks this buy — nothing scrapable left at that line" — so the refusal is explained before you click, and the server still refuses honestly
Feed lines for the floor change and the overflow-policy switch now mention the floor when one is set

entries.title: No surprises at the scrap pile
features: When auto-scrap is on and a buy would have to sell spares to fit, the buy button now says so before you click it: a gold ♻️ pre-flight line under the price — "♻️ this buy scraps 1 spare card (~$4.48–$6.06)" — with a live read of the real scrap pool

The hint appears on Market listings, buylist shop shelves, and Local Deals cards, and stays silent when there's room or the policy is set to refuse — it only speaks when clicking would actually cost you cardboard

entries.title: The overflow policy
features: New choice on the Storage page — ♻️ When the shelf is full: Refuse the buy (the old behavior: deliveries bounce, nothing you own is touched) or Auto-scrap for room (your cheapest spare bulk sells to the scrap dealer at 8¢ on the dollar until the delivery fits)

Auto-scrap honors the policy on Market buys, shop shelves, Local deals, and Trades — pack rips, resale lots, estate lots, and storage hauls make room the same way, and the feed records every auto-scrap with the cash it paid you

Favorites are always spared, and so is anything spoken for: binder pockets, shop cases, bulk boxes, grab bags, and franchise shelves are excluded from the scrap pool — if only protected cards remain, the delivery is refused with an honest "not even the scrap pile could make room"
The scrap rate is now one shared constant — a haul sort and an overflow scrap always pay the same street rate

entries.title: The vault & the watchman
features: The 🏆 vault rider now pays off in the insurance system too: slabs stored off-site are immune to the whole disaster roll — roof leaks, coffee spills, attic heat, and break-ins all pass them by (a break-in that finds the vault stocked says so in the feed)
Each rented locker adds a $0.75/wk storage surcharge to the insurance premium draft (more doors, more watch) — the surcharge shows in the weekly line, the draft feed entry, and the Insurance panel

Fixed the disaster clock: the daily 3% disaster roll was actually rolling every 20-second tick (the once-per-day guard was never written) — now it rolls once per game day, the day is consumed even when nothing is exposed to the rolled event, and forced diagnostic rolls can't fish for juicier targets

entries.title: The full-shelf early warning
features: Collection and Inventory now carry a capacity strip once your shelf crosses 75% full — amber while there's still room ("📦 Shelf filling up — 75/100 raw cards stored"), red and shouting when it's full, so the first refused buy is never a surprise
The strip names the slab rack too when the vault or dresser spots are maxed, and carries a 🗄 Rent a locker → shortcut straight to the Storage & Auctions locker desk

entries.title: Storage & the vault
features: Your collection has a roof: the bedroom shelf holds 100 raw cards free, and every acquisition path — packs, market buys, shop shelves, parking-lot deals, resale lots, estate lots, trades, and storage-unit hauls — checks the racks before the cash moves

Rent storage lockers at the facility (Small 5×5 +100 slots $15/mo · Medium 10×10 +250 $30/mo · Large 10×20 +600 $55/mo, billed weekly with a first month up front) and turn them back in when you downsize — only when they're empty

Graded slabs don't stack: two live on the dresser free, and the 🏆 vault rider policy ($12/mo) rents 25 insured slots under camera and glass — slabs in hauls go straight back under the blanket without it

A full shelf refuses deliveries instead of losing them: market buys bounce with the count ("200/200 cards stored"), pack rips leave the overflow in the wrapper, haul sorts scrap what the racks can't take — and a warning in the feed tells you exactly what got left behind

The Storage page (now Storage & Auctions) opens with a live capacity meter for raw cards and slabs, the locker rental desk, and the vault rider policy — rent drafts land in the feed and the weekly P&L

entries.title: The polish pass
features: Buylist sales now count toward unlocks, achievements, and your sales record — they were silently never written to the books (the "Make 3 sales" counter ignored every NPC-shop sale)
Fixed a routing bug where the vendor-table stock API was shadowed by the booth-detail route — stocking your convention table or show booth never worked and always answered "No show running"
Stale or mistyped links (old bookmarks, #/ebay, #/set with no set picked) now bounce home with a toast instead of a silent blank page
The BidBay To-ship queue refreshes live — a sale that lands while you watch the page no longer waits for a navigate-away to appear

entries.title: Shipping & condition disputes
features: A BidBay sale isn't money until it ships: every sold order waits in the new To-ship queue — pick 📬 Economy / 📦 Standard / 🚚 Priority postage (real costs booked to overhead) and pack from your actual supplies stock
Ship it bare and the buyer's corner test decides your fate — damaged-arrival disputes refund the buyer IN FULL and the card never comes back
📷 Pack-out photos + decent packing are your evidence: win a dispute and payout releases minus a goodwill fee; lose one and the 1★ lands in your feedback rating
Economy parcels with no tracking can vanish entirely — bubble mailers join the Supplies shop as the fourth stock item

entries.title: Unlock quest counters
features: The sidebar's 🔒 next-goal hints now show live progress — "🔒 Make 5 sales 2/5" — counting up as you play until the lock opens
Cash goals track your saved dollars and follower goals your stream following, each updating live with the same 15-second heartbeat as the rest of the game

entries.title: What's New panel
features: In-game changelog — the sidebar's ✨ What's New row (with a badge when you haven't caught up) opens the version history so returning players can see everything added since their last session
Seen-tracking is per save: catch up once and the badge clears, and every future update re-badges itself

entries.title: Next-unlock hints
features: Locked views now advertise themselves — one subtle 🔒 row per sidebar section names the nearest goal there ("Make 5 sales", "Save $400", "Gather 5 followers") with the target view in the tooltip
Hints advance live as you play and vanish when a section is fully unlocked

entries.title: Organized sidebar & progressive unlocks
features: The nav is regrouped into six clean sections (COLLECT · MARKET · EVENTS · BUSINESS · PLAY · SYSTEM) with every surface sorted into place — the duplicated BUSINESS header is gone
New saves ease in: Pawn/Yard unlock at 3 sales, Local Deals/Storage at 5, BidBay at 8, Live Shopping at 12, Card Shop/Resale Desk at $500/$400 saved, Stream at 5 followers
🔓 unlock toasts celebrate each first reveal; veterans see everything immediately

entries.title: Facebook Marketplace & Craigslist
features: 🪧 Local Deals — the wild west: NPC listings at 0.4×–3.5× market with 🐟 counterfeit tells, named parking-lot meetups, ~1-in-8 no-shows both directions
Counterfeit risk: skip the in-person corner test and a fake is yours forever (buylist shops take them for a dollar); $15 on-the-lot inspection removes the risk
Sell from your binder with your own post — midnight 🌙 lowballs included; every deal is cash, no fees, no paper trail

entries.title: Card shows as an attendee — the floor
features: Every NPC dealer table has a person with a mood (😄 → 😠) driving hidden rigidity, patience, and their buy offers on your binder
Haggle: meet their floor for a handshake, land close for a midpoint counter, lowball a grump and the table goes cold for the show
Sell for cash or +8% store credit (silos per dealer), push once for more, or drop cards in PSA's 📦 grade-and-go box from the floor

entries.title: Insurance
features: Three policies (Starter/Collector/Museum) with weekly premiums sized to your live appraisal — raw cards, slabs, and sealed
A ~3% daily chance of roof leaks, coffee spills, attic heat waves, or break-ins: raw slips a condition step, slabs drop a grade, thieves take slabs outright
7-day waiting periods, lapse & grace rules, itemized claims — and the accountant flags uninsured collections

entries.title: Starting tutorial
features: A five-step welcome walkthrough for fresh saves — the $1,000 loop, collecting, grading, the hunt surfaces, the empire
Finishing or skipping flips a per-save flag so it never nags; Settings can replay it; resetting your save resets the tour

entries.title: Hover-to-zoom everywhere
features: Every card image in the game zooms on hover with a floating preview and opens the full detail modal on click — Collection, Market, BidBay, Pawn, Buylist, Grading, Wishlist, Binders, hauls, peeks, lots, Home strips, Set pages, reveals, and live rooms
